context.exploration_scope: Second real-operational-mode Evolution run: added explicit Drift stage distinguishing "any change" (Trigger) from "genuinely new discrepancy not already known from E35..E45" (Drift); Gate/Execution skipped when no new drift, per this phase's explicit core rule

problem: E45 established Trigger-first operational mode but only distinguished triggered-vs-not; it did not yet separate "any change" from "a genuinely new, not-already-known discrepancy" -- E46 was asked to add that distinction and confirm the skip rule holds under it too.

decision.decision_summary: Trigger (E40 baseline): 0 changes -- triggered=false. Drift (excluding known E35..E45 conditions): 0 genuinely new discrepancies. Gate and Execution explicitly SKIPPED (not run, not merely empty) -- no real new change to react to. 0 code modifications.

action.action_summary: Fresh Trigger check against E40's fixed baseline; explicit Drift stage excluding already-known E35..E45 conditions; Gate/Execution conditionally skipped; Verification always run; 0 new Evolution mechanism designed.

result.note: No genuinely new project change since E40 -- correctly skipped Gate/Execution rather than re-running them, confirming E45's skip rule holds under the added Drift-vs-Trigger distinction.

cause.root_cause_summary: E45 proved the Trigger-first skip rule for "any change vs. none"; it had not yet been exercised against the finer distinction of "changed but already-known" vs. "genuinely new" -- E46 closes that gap.

lesson: Distinguishing "any drift" from "genuinely new drift" (excluding already-known, already-recorded conditions like the GPU bottleneck or the semantic-quality gate) prevents the operational loop from re-surfacing the same known-DEFERRED conditions as if they were fresh problems every run.
